mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS has been above 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and consumer credit (RSAFS) indicate a contraction in household spending and investment, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by high consumer spending (RSAFS above 700,000) and rising housing starts (HOUST above 1,250), the S&P 500 tends to underperform as the economy approaches a peak, leading to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where RSAFS > 700,000 and HOUST > 1,250.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 for two consecutive months, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output that reduces corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO has been below 100 for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the past 6 months indicates a tightening labor market that boosts corporate hiring and wage growth, supporting higher earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where UNRATE has declined for 6 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average indicates expanding manufacturing output that supports corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where UNRATE has been above 4.5% for two consecutive months.
